# FDG8038

> DO use the “Dictionary” suffix in names of abstractions implementing `IDictionary` or `IDictionary<TKey,TValue>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.4.1 Naming Custom Collections.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

The text has no body. Test profile: none, because CA1710 also enforces the other suffixes of Table 3-5, and chapter 3 is off in the test profile. CA1710 reports a type that implements IDictionary&lt;TKey, TValue> or IDictionary, also through a base class such as Dictionary&lt;TKey, TValue> because the package sets dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = false (see FDG3048; probe with SDK 10.0.403), and whose name does not end with Dictionary. It also accepts Collection, so coverage is partial. FDG3057 is the same guideline in chapter 3. Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 has no code fix.
